title: Target header card under-reports planned exposures and integration time by the loop multiplier - including for every sequence the app's own Quick-Start Wizard builds
what_happened: I ran the Quick-Start Wizard end to end (M31, 120s, count 10). It produced a Capture Loop with repeatCount 10 containing a single 'Light 1 x 120s' exposure node, all under the M31 TargetHeader. The toolbar reported '10 frames' and the DB stored estimated_duration_mins = 20 (correct). The M31 target header card on the same screen reported 'Ready / 1 planned exposures - 2m'. Ten-fold understatement of both the frame count and the integration time, on the card the user reads to decide whether the night's plan is right.
expected: '10 planned exposures - 20m', matching the toolbar frame count and the stored estimate.
repro: Sequencer > Templates > Quick-Start Wizard. Step 1: RA 0.712, Dec 41.27, name M31. Next through steps 2-5 with defaults. Create Sequence. Read the M31 target card status line, then scroll down to see 'Capture Loop x10 > Light 1 x 120s', then read the toolbar frame counter.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-52-qsbuilt.png ('1 planned exposures - 2m' + toolbar '10 frames'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-54-qstree2.png (Capture Loop x10 containing Light 1x120s), sqlite dump of sequence_nodes for sequence_id=3 showing Loop {"conditionType":"count","repeatCount":10} as the parent of the TakeExposure {"count":1}
proposed_fix: Give visit() a multiplier argument and multiply by LoopNode.repeatCount for count-type loops, exactly as Sequence._countExposures does at sequence_state.dart:168-188. Better: delete _calculateTargetPlan and reuse the model's counting so the two can never diverge again.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end to end. Ran the Quick-Start Wizard (RA 0.712, Dec 41.27, name M31, 120s, defaults through steps 2-5) and pressed Create Sequence. The built tree is 'Capture Loop x10' containing 'Light 1 x 120s' (sbv-52-tree2.png); the toolbar frame counter reads '10 frames' and the M31 target header card on the same screen reads 'Ready / 1 planned exposures - 2m' (sbv-50-m31seq.png). Saving it stored estimated_duration_mins = 20 for that sequence (sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-build-verify/data/skotiq.db 'select id,name,estimated_duration_mins from sequences' -> 2|M31 Sequence|20). So toolbar and DB agree at 10 frames / 20m and only the target card is 10x low. Code matches the named location: target_header_card.dart _calculateTargetPlan's visit() (~lines 675-706) recurses into childIds with no loop multiplier, unlike Sequence._countExposures (sequence_state.dart:168-188) which multiplies by LoopNode.repeatCount for count-type loops. Severity corrected P1->P2: it is a false plan summary but display-only, and the correct figure is shown in the toolbar beside it.

title: Exposure Triggers dialog lets you add and Save a trigger, then silently discards it when the selected node cannot hold triggers
what_happened: With the root 'Sequence' InstructionSet selected I clicked the toolbar bell (Exposure Triggers). The dialog opened, 'Add Trigger' created 'Guiding RMS > 2.0" -> Pause & Recalibrate', and Save closed the dialog with no error. Reopening the dialog showed 'No triggers configured'. Repeating the identical steps with a Take Exposures node selected persisted the trigger correctly. The button is enabled regardless of selection and the dialog gives no indication which node it is editing.
expected: Either disable the toolbar button (with a tooltip: 'select an exposure node') when the selection cannot hold triggers, or tell the user on Save that nothing was stored. Silently accepting and dropping a safety trigger is the worst of the three options - a user who set 'abort if guiding RMS > 2"' would believe they are protected.
repro: Sequencer > Builder > click the root 'Sequence' row > toolbar bell icon > Add Trigger > Save > click the bell again: 'No triggers configured'. Now add a Take Exposures node, select it, and repeat: the trigger is there on reopen.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-74-addtrigger.png (trigger created), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-76-trigreopen.png ('No triggers configured' after Save+reopen, root selected), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-78-trig2.png (same steps with an exposure node selected: trigger persists)
proposed_fix: Resolve the target exposure node up front; if none, disable the toolbar action and put the reason in the tooltip. Show the owning node's name in the dialog subtitle so the user knows what they are editing.
verdict_reasoning: The user-visible defect is real but the stated cause is wrong. REFUTED as written: with the root 'Sequence' InstructionSet selected in a sequence that contained a Take Exposures node, I added 'Guiding RMS > 2.0" -> Pause & Recalibrate', pressed Save, and on reopening the dialog the trigger was still there (sbv-27-trigreopen.png). Selection is irrelevant. CONFIRMED under the real condition: on a sequence with NO ExposureNode (fresh New Sequence, 1 node / 0 steps) the identical steps - Add Trigger (sbv-31-trigadd2.png), Save, reopen - show 'No triggers configured' (sbv-33-trigreopen2.png) with no error. Code explains both: sequence_toolbar.dart:166-195 openExposureTriggers writes the result into every ExposureNode in the sequence via `for (final node in current.nodes.values.whereType<ExposureNode>())`, and currentExposureTriggers() (:156-164) reads from the first ExposureNode; with zero exposure nodes both are no-ops while the success snackbar still fires. The proposed fix (resolve the target exposure node up front, disable with a reason when none) is still the right fix. Severity corrected P1->P2: it only drops the trigger on a sequence that has no exposure node at all, i.e. one that cannot image anything yet.

title: Mosaic Wizard invents a camera field of view and plans the whole mosaic from it, while the framing dialog on the same screen correctly refuses to guess
what_happened: With no equipment profile configured, the Mosaic Wizard's Plan summary states 'Panel size: 1.00 deg x 0.67 deg' and derives 'Active panels 9 / Grid 3x3 / Est. time 2.3 h / Total exposures 90' from it. Those degrees are the hardcoded field defaults _panelWidthArcmin = 60.0 / _panelHeightArcmin = 40.0, not anything measured from the user's rig. The 'Frame target' dialog, reachable from the same Builder screen, handles the identical missing data honestly: 'No equipment profile with a focal length - set one in Settings to size the framing box.'
expected: Say the FOV is unknown and require a focal length / sensor size (or an explicit override) before quoting a panel size, panel count and total time as facts.
repro: Sequencer > Builder (no equipment profile) > toolbar grid icon (Plan Mosaic). Read 'Panel size' in the Plan summary. Then select a Target node and click 'Frame target' and read its warning.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-79-mosaic.png ('Panel size: 1.00 deg x 0.67 deg'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-22-frame.png (framing dialog admits it cannot size the box)
proposed_fix: Initialise the panel size from the active equipment profile's focal length + sensor dimensions. When that is unavailable, show 'unknown' with the same wording the framing dialog uses and disable 'Load into Sequencer' / 'Create mosaic project' until it is supplied.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with no equipment profile configured. The Mosaic Wizard's Plan summary states 'Active panels 9 / Grid 3x3 / Panel size: 1.00 deg x 0.67 deg / Overlap 10% / Est. time (14m/panel x 10 subs): 2.3 h / Total exposures: 90' (sbv-43-mosaic.png). Those degrees are exactly the hardcoded field initialisers _panelWidthArcmin = 60.0 and _panelHeightArcmin = 40.0 at mosaic_wizard_dialog.dart:64-65; initState (:105-129) sets only _centerRa/_centerDec and never reads an equipment profile, focal length or sensor size. The contrast claim also holds: the Frame-target dialog on the same Builder screen says 'Field of view unknown - No equipment profile with a focal length - set one in Settings to size the framing box.' (sbv-44-frame.png). One mitigating fact the finding omits: the panel size IS user-editable in the wizard's Advanced section (callback at :891-898), so this is an invented default presented as fact rather than an unchangeable one. Severity P2 upheld.
